tasks.brief:
Implementation constraints: Create src/services/storage.py. Use ONLY stdlib: json, os, tempfile, logging. Do NOT use any third-party libraries. Read TESTCHAT_DATA env var at call time inside load_snapshot and save_snapshot, not at import time. Do NOT use threading or async.

Behavioral specification: Implement two functions. load_snapshot() -> list[dict]: Read TESTCHAT_DATA env var; default to 'data/threads.json'. If file missing, unreadable, or invalid JSON, return [] and log a warning (logging.warning). Otherwise parse JSON and return the list. save_snapshot(threads: list[dict]) -> None: Read TESTCHAT_DATA env var; default to 'data/threads.json'. Ensure parent directory exists (os.makedirs with exist_ok=True). Write threads as JSON to a temp file in the same directory using tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile, then os.replace() the temp file onto the target path for atomicity. If save fails, log a warning and do not raise.

Acceptance condition: load_snapshot returns [] on missing/corrupt file; save_snapshot atomically writes and overwrites; env var is read at call time.

Implementation constraints: Create src/api/threads.py. Import FastAPI's APIRouter, Pydantic's BaseModel. Import load_snapshot and save_snapshot from src.services.storage. Do NOT import anything else from the app. Define two Pydantic models: ThreadSnapshot (id: int, title: str, messages: list[dict], model: str = '', locked: bool = False) and ThreadsPayload (threads: list[ThreadSnapshot]).

Behavioral specification: Create an APIRouter instance. Define GET /api/v1/threads that calls load_snapshot() and returns {'threads': result}. Define PUT /api/v1/threads that accepts ThreadsPayload, converts payload.threads to plain dicts, calls save_snapshot, returns {'status': 'ok'}. Define DELETE /api/v1/threads that calls save_snapshot([]) and returns {'status': 'ok'}. Pydantic automatically returns 422 on malformed input.

Acceptance condition: GET returns loaded threads; PUT saves and returns ok; DELETE clears and returns ok; 422 on bad input.

Implementation constraints: Edit src/main.py. Add a third defensive try/except import block, identical in shape to existing chat/models import blocks. Inside the block, import src.api.threads and attach its router to the FastAPI app instance. Do NOT change any other code. Do NOT add new imports outside the try/except.

Behavioral specification: Locate the existing try/except import blocks for chat and models. Add a new block that imports src.api.threads and mounts the router. The router mount must be additive and not break existing routes.

Acceptance condition: The app starts successfully with the threads router mounted; existing routes still work; no import errors.

Implementation constraints: Edit src/static/app.js. Four small anchored edits only. Do NOT rewrite the file. Do NOT add new dependencies. Use fetch API for persistence calls.

Behavioral specification: (a) Add persistThreads() helper: fetch PUT /api/v1/threads with JSON.stringify({threads: threads.map(t => ({id: t.id, title: t.title, messages: t.messages, model: t.model || '', locked: !!t.locked}))}), fire-and-forget (.catch swallowed). (b) Replace bare createThread() bootstrap with fetch GET /api/v1/threads: on non-empty threads array, rebuild state (threads = data.threads with messages/model/locked; threadCounter = max id; activeThreadId = first thread's id; renderThreadMessages + restoreThreadModelState + renderSidebar); on empty array OR fetch error, fall back to createThread(). (c) Call persistThreads() in the 'done' event handler, immediately after the two messages are pushed. (d) Call persistThreads() at the end of createThread().

Acceptance condition: Persistence helper exists and is called correctly; hydration on startup works; UI tests pass including test_threads_survive_reload.
